 # ===========================================================================
 # Character: everything in Rian is an EXPRESSION that yields a value — `if`,
-# `match`, and blocks included. There are no statements that don't produce a
+# `case`, and blocks included. There are no statements that don't produce a

 # Single-clause function. The typed head IS the type boundary — no separate
 # signature line is needed when there is exactly one clause.
-fn add(x i64, y i64) i64 := x + y

 # Block body: a `;`/newline-separated sequence of bindings whose value is the
 # LAST expression (implicit return). Bodies open after the return type and
 # close with `end`.
-fn double_then_inc(n i64) i64
+def double_then_inc(n Int64) Int64
   d := n * 2          # `:=` is a single-assignment binding, never mutation
   d + 1               # the final expression is the function's value
 end
 
 # `:=` is single-assignment and irrefutable. Re-using a name SHADOWS the old
 # binding (a fresh value), it does not mutate it. Mutation is a different
 # operator, `<-`, and is capability-gated (see 04_capabilities.rian).
-fn shadow_demo(n i64) i64
+def shadow_demo(n Int64) Int64
   x := n + 1
   x := x * 10         # shadow: a NEW `x`, the old one is untouched
   x
 end

+def sign(n Int64) Int64 := if n >= 0 do 1 else -1 end
 
 # else-if chains read top to bottom.

+def grade(s Int64) String :=
   if s >= 90 do "A"
   else if s >= 80 do "B"

 # Guards are a RESTRICTED, pure, total sublanguage — the intersection of

+def cmp(_, _)             := Greater
 
 # Union narrowing: a guard that narrows a union lowers to a GUARD on Elixir
 # but a PATTERN ARM on Rust (Rust narrows enums structurally). Same source,
 # two idiomatic shapes.
-fn show(i64 | str) str

 # Exhaustiveness is enforced: GUARDED clauses do not count, so a guard-only
 # function needs an unguarded fallback. `max2`'s second clause is the
 # unguarded backstop that makes it total on both targets.
-fn max2(i64, i64) i64
-fn max2(a, b) when a >= b := a
-fn max2(a, b)             := b
+def max2(Int64, Int64) Int64
+def max2(a, b) when a >= b := a
+def max2(a, b)             := b

 # Elixir relies on `FunctionClauseError`.
 @partial
-fn unwrap(Option(T)) T
-fn unwrap(Some(x)) := x
+def unwrap(Option(T)) T
+def unwrap(Some(x)) := x

-#   val        | i64 byval | &str   | &[f64]        | &Shape

 # `val` (default): a read-only borrow. On Rust this is `&Shape` and uses the
 # idiomatic borrowed forms (`&str` not `&String`, `&[T]` not `&Vec<T>`). On the
 # BEAM a `val` is freely shareable — usable any number of times. That is WHY
 # `r * r` below is legal: `r` flows from a `val` parameter.
-fn area(s val Shape) f64
-fn area(Circle(r)) := 3.14159265 * r * r       # r used twice — fine, it's val
-fn area(Square(s)) := s * s
+def area(s val Shape) Float64
+def area(Circle(r)) := 3.14159265 * r * r       # r used twice — fine, it's val
+def area(Square(s)) := s * s
 
 # `iso`: a unique, owned handle. On Rust this MOVES (`fn consume(s: Shape)`).
 # On the BEAM it is a USE-ONCE linear value: using it twice along a path is a
 # compile error. This catches "used after consumed" with no borrow checker.
-fn consume(s iso Shape) f64 := area(s)         # ok: `s` consumed exactly once
+def consume(s iso Shape) Float64 := area(s)         # ok: `s` consumed exactly once
 
 # The linearity check would REJECT this (iso `s` used twice):
-#   fn bad(s iso Shape) f64 := area(s) + area(s)   # error: {"s", 2}
+#   def bad(s iso Shape) Float64 := area(s) + area(s)   # error: {"s", 2}

 # Rust-superset feature, honestly fenced off rather than faked.
-fn scale(s ref Vec(f64), k f64) Vec(f64) := mul_each(s, k)   # &mut Vec<f64> on Rust
+def scale(s ref Vec(Float64), k Float64) Vec(Float64) := mul_each(s, k)   # &mut Vec<f64> on Rust
 
 # `tag`: identity only (a pid/ref on the BEAM, a borrow on Rust). Shareable;
 # you can observe identity but the value's contents are not owned.
-fn same(a tag Shape, b tag Shape) bool := a == b
+def same(a tag Shape, b tag Shape) Bool := a == b
 
 # Field capabilities work too: a struct field marked `iso` makes the whole
 # type non-`Clone` on Rust (only `Debug`), because the field is unique.
-struct Buffer(data iso Vec(u8), len val i64)
+struct Buffer(data iso Vec(UInt8), len val Int64)

 # node the parser produces and is BRANCH-AWARE for `if` — a value consumed once

 # legal, while a double-use within a single arm is still rejected. The same
-# `max` rule extends to `match`-expression bodies once they lower through this
-# checker (today `match` is handled at the clause level, not as a counted node).
+# `max` rule extends to `case`-expression bodies once they lower through this
+# checker (today `case` is handled at the clause level, not as a counted node).
